title: Helpful Resources
intro: Here are trusted resources to help you learn more about PrEP, find a provider, and get help paying for your medication. All of these are free to access.

resources.name: CDC PrEP Information
resources.description: Trusted information about PrEP from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, including how it works, who it's for, and how to get it.

resources.name: PrEP Facts
resources.description: Easy-to-understand information about PrEP options, including answers to common questions and real stories from people who use PrEP.

resources.name: HIV.gov - PrEP
resources.description: The federal government's main resource for HIV information, including a section on PrEP with the latest updates and guidance.

resources.name: PrEP Locator
resources.description: Search for clinics and providers near you that offer PrEP. You can filter by location, insurance accepted, and services offered.

resources.name: GetYourPrEP
resources.description: Find PrEP providers, learn about getting started, and connect with support services in your area.

resources.name: HRSA Health Center Finder
resources.description: Find a federally qualified health center near you. These centers provide care on a sliding fee scale and many offer PrEP services.

resources.name: Ready, Set, PrEP
resources.description: A federal program that provides PrEP medication at no cost to people who don't have insurance coverage for prescription drugs. You can enroll online or by phone.

resources.name: Gilead Advancing Access
resources.description: Gilead Sciences offers copay assistance for people with insurance, as well as free medication for eligible people without insurance. Covers tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (Truvada), tenofovir alafenamide (Descovy), and lenacapavir (Yeztugo).

resources.name: ViiV Patient Assistance
resources.description: ViiV Healthcare offers patient assistance programs for people who are prescribed cabotegravir (Apretude). Includes help for both insured and uninsured individuals.
